skill.name: animation-vocabulary
skill.description: Identifies precise web animation and motion-design terms from plain-language descriptions, then distinguishes close alternatives using a curated glossary.
skill.summary: Turn a vague motion description into the correct animation term.
skill.author: emilkowalski

content.value_statement: Vague motion descriptions make design discussions and AI prompts unclear. This skill maps those descriptions to precise terms and explains close alternatives.
actual_capabilities: Maps plain-language motion descriptions to terms in its curated animation glossary.
Returns the strongest matching term before any alternatives.
Distinguishes related concepts such as morph, crossfade, and shared element transition.
Combines glossary terms when no single entry fully describes an effect.
Provides concise, glossary-based definitions for identified terms.
limitations: It names effects but does not design, code, or test animations.
It is limited to terms included in the bundled glossary.
Ambiguous descriptions may require context about the element, trigger, or movement.
It does not provide framework-specific implementation guidance.

use_cases.title: Clarify a design review
use_cases.description: Identify the accepted term for a motion effect before documenting interface feedback.

use_cases.title: Improve an AI request
use_cases.description: Replace a vague visual description with precise animation terminology in a prompt.

use_cases.title: Standardize team language
use_cases.description: Resolve competing names for an interaction and compare the closest glossary terms.

prompt_templates.title: Name one effect
prompt_templates.prompt: What is the animation called when [describe what moves, changes, or appears]?
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a direct term for one visible effect.

prompt_templates.title: Identify from behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Name this interface motion: [element] responds to [trigger] by [movement]. Include one concise definition.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the trigger and movement are known.

prompt_templates.title: Compare possible terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify the best term for [effect]. Compare it with up to two close alternatives and explain the differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several animation concepts may fit.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a complex effect
prompt_templates.prompt: Describe [complex motion sequence] using only glossary terms. Separate entrance, movement, timing, easing, and interaction concepts where applicable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a sequence combines multiple animation techniques.

output_examples.input: Cards appear one after another with a short delay.
output_examples.output: Stagger - Animate several items one after another with a small delay between each, creating a cascade.

output_examples.input: An image fades away while another appears in the same place.
output_examples.output: Crossfade - One element fades out as another fades in, in the same spot.

output_examples.input: A thumbnail expands into a detail view while remaining visually connected.
output: Shared element transition - An element travels and transforms from one position into another, like a thumbnail expanding into a card.
Close alternate: View transition, when the browser connects states or pages.

best_practices: Describe the trigger, moving element, direction, timing, and final state.
Ask for alternatives when the effect could match several terms.
Use the returned term in design documentation or implementation prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not request production animation code from this naming skill.
Do not expect terms that are absent from the bundled glossary.
Do not provide only subjective words when visible behavior can be described.

faq.question: Can this skill build an animation?
faq.answer: No. It identifies and explains animation terms but does not produce implementation code.

faq.question: What kinds of motion can it identify?
faq.answer: It covers entrances, exits, transforms, transitions, scroll effects, interaction feedback, easing, springs, loops, performance, and motion principles.

faq.question: What happens when several terms match?
faq.answer: It presents the best match first, then compares up to two close alternatives.

faq.question: Can it identify an effect outside the glossary?
faq.answer: It states when no exact term exists and may describe the effect by combining available terms.

faq.question: Does it support framework-specific terminology?
faq.answer: The glossary focuses on general web and interface animation concepts, not framework APIs.

faq.question: How should I describe an unknown animation?
faq.answer: State what moves, what triggers it, how its speed changes, and what the element does at the end.
